third_reason: ICP-AES mineral composition assay of brown rice from near-isogenic plant lines; 'cold tolerance at booting stage' is the rice plant's agronomic trait. No human, no ingestion. EXCLUDE (agri / name-only) per §2 conditions 1-2.

Maternal brown rice diet in mice; UCP1, thermogenic gene expression and heat production are genuine thermogenesis outcomes, but the subjects are mice, so §2 condition 1 (human, in vivo) fails. EXCLUDE (animal). Flagged as the record most likely to be misread as an include on outcome alone.

Foliar nano-delivery of melatonin/GSH to reduce cadmium in rice grain; 'brown rice' is the plant tissue compartment and 'energy expenditure' refers to the plant's phenylpropanoid metabolism. No human, no ingestion. EXCLUDE (agri) per §2 conditions 1-2.

Human crossover trial, but the exposure of interest is anthocyanin-rich black rice; brown rice is the 0 mg-anthocyanin comparator, so §2 condition 4 (the food is the exposure of interest) fails for this key. Outcomes are cognition, IL-6 and microvascular blood flow/blood pressure in an ageing-vascular-function framing with no thermal readout, which §2.3 (vascular bed / reactivity probes) makes `no-thermal`; the vascular bed is not named and no local thermal hyperaemia is reported. Two independent grounds, so exclude rather than uncertain.

Human acute trial of whey vs a plant protein blend in which brown rice protein is one of three components (pea, brown rice, pumpkin seed), with no brown-rice-specific readout — §3 mixed/whole-diet rule. REE and RER are measured but framed as postprandial metabolism, appetite and subsequent energy intake, never as thermogenesis, DIT, TEF or a thermogenic effect, so §2.3(B) is not met. EXCLUDE (no-thermal).

§3 animal: buckwheat polyphenol 600 mg/kg p.o. in rats subjected to repeated cerebral ischemia. §2 condition 1 fails; independently, the only perfusion measure is hippocampal blood flow by laser Doppler, which is organ-specific (cerebral) perfusion measured for a non-thermal purpose and is no-thermal under §2.3(A).

§2 condition 4 + §3 name-only (contamination). This is the closest call in the batch and I considered the include case: 20 healthy adults, randomised double-blind placebo-controlled crossover, oral ingestion of a boiled-buckwheat-flour meal, with body temperature and sweat secretion recorded for 4 h — conditions 1, 2 and 3 all hold. Condition 4 does not: the exposure of interest is the atropine/scopolamine mixture added to the meal (a Datura-derived contaminant, not a buckwheat constituent under the §3 isolated-constituent rule), and the placebo arm ate the same buckwheat meal, so buckwheat is held constant across arms and no thermal effect can be attributed to it. The thermal variables are anticholinergic toxicity endpoints for an ARfD derivation. §3 lists contamination studies under name-only.

§3 animal: ovariectomised rats fed high-fat diets with buckwheat sprout powder for 12 weeks. Skin temperature and energy expenditure are measured, so this would be on-construct in a human — but §2 condition 1 fails and the animal code is decisive.

§3 name-only / agri: description of the Tartary buckwheat genomics database (TBD). 'Rutin can enhance blood flow' is a background claim about the crop's nutritional value with no measurement and no subject; no human ingestion study is reported (§2 conditions 1-4 all fail).

§3 agri: metabolomics and transcriptomics of the phenylalanine pathway in two Tartary buckwheat landraces after cold treatment at the seedling stage, for cold-tolerance breeding. Plant cold stress, no human ingestion (§2 conditions 1-2 fail).

§2.3(B) energy expenditure: randomised crossover in 20 healthy volunteers with a 7-day buckwheat diet — conditions 1, 2 and 4 hold, but condition 3 fails. Resting metabolic rate appears only as the denominator used to size each volunteer's provided diet, not as a measured thermogenic outcome, which §2.3(B) codes no-thermal. Measured outcomes are subjective hunger/satiety (not thermal sensation), gut microbiota, plasma lipids, glucose, insulin, urea, homocysteine and targeted metabolomics. No temperature, thermogenesis, TEF or cutaneous/limb perfusion readout.

§3 no-thermal: 55 patients with insulin-dependent diabetes underwent carbohydrate food loading, buckwheat named as one low-glycaemic-index food. Human ingestion holds, but the 2-h postprandial measurements are glycaemia, C-peptide, insulin, glucagon, hydrocortisone and STH — no thermal readout; 'metabolic stress' here is a counter-regulatory hormone response, not thermogenesis or the thermic effect of food under §2.3(B), and 'systemic blood flow' refers to glucose entering the circulation, not a §2.3(A) vascular bed.

Agronomic comparison of Welsh onion cultivars under winter cultivation: electrolyte leakage, malondialdehyde, chlorophyll, photosynthetic rate, bolting rate and yield. 'Cold tolerance' is the crop's, not a human's. EXCLUDE (agri) per §2 conditions 1-3. This is green onion's only L2 hit, so the key's L2' is 0 on this judgment; the record is nonetheless unambiguously plant agronomy.

Human study (n=8), but roasted green tea appears only as the 25 mL control mouth-rinse against Gymnema sylvestre; the exposure of interest is sweet-taste suppression during a glucose load, so §2 condition 4 fails and the tea is a rinse rather than an intake (§2 condition 2). The vascular outcome is celiac-artery / gastrointestinal blood flow by ultrasonography — organ-specific splanchnic perfusion measured for a digestive purpose, which §2.3 (vascular bed) makes `no-thermal`; no skin or limb perfusion, no temperature, no thermal sensation. EXCLUDE. Noting for the record that this is hojicha's only L2 hit, so this key's L2' is 0 on the strength of this judgment — but all three failure grounds are stated explicitly in the abstract, not inferred.

§3 no-thermal: the human arm (volunteers given candy containing L. plantarum K8 lysates) measures skin hydration, horny layer thickness and TEWL only — barrier function, not a §2.3 thermal outcome; the sentence about skin controlling body temperature is background, not a measurement. Also the exposure is a kimchi-derived bacterial lysate, which is not the food, a food-form of it, or its principal dietary constituent under §2 condition 2 / §3.

§2 condition 3 fails: 46 human patients ingesting a kimchi/cheonggukjang probiotic product, so conditions 1, 2 and 4 hold, and scalp perfusion would be a cutaneous bed within §2.3(A) — but improved scalp blood flow is only the stated hypothesis, never measured. The measured outcomes are hair count and thickness by Triple Scope System, and the conclusion attributes them to anagen-phase initiation. No perfusion, temperature or thermal-sensation readout, so no-thermal.

§3 agri: transcriptome and antioxidant-metabolism response of the growing kimchi cabbage plant (Brassica rapa ssp. pekinensis) to cold stress, framed as improving crop cold tolerance. The plant, not the fermented food, and no human ingestion (§2 conditions 1-2 fail).

§3 animal: male C57BL/6 and gnotobiotic mice fed a high-fat diet with kimchi. §2 condition 1 fails. Independently, 'energy expenditure' appears only in a background clause about hypothalamic function; the measured endpoints are body weight, fat mass, cytokines, gliosis, BBB integrity and microbiota — a body-composition/obesity framing that §2.3(B) codes no-thermal.

§3 invitro: differentiated T37i brown adipocytes in culture. The paper is explicitly thermogenesis-framed, which is what makes it the tempting record in this batch, but there is no human and no ingestion — outcomes are cell viability, intracellular triglyceride, lipid accumulation and thermogenic gene/protein expression, and the stated objective is anti-obesity. §2 conditions 1 and 2 fail, and §2.3(B)'s thermogenesis framing cannot rescue a cell-culture study.

Genome sequencing of the kiwi bird (Apteryx, a New Zealand ratite), not the fruit Actinidia. No human, no ingestion, no thermal readout; 'energy expenditure' appears only as a gene-enrichment category. EXCLUDE (animal / name-only) per §2 conditions 1-3.
Avian malaria (Plasmodium elongatum) in birds and mosquitoes; 'brown kiwi' names the bird host. No human ingestion, no thermal outcome. EXCLUDE (animal) per §2 EXCLUDE list.

Bovine uterine metagenomics; the token 'kiwi' comes only from the STAMP software URL (kiwi.cs.dal.ca). Rectal temperature is a cow case-definition criterion, not a food ingestion outcome. EXCLUDE (name-only / animal) per §2 conditions 1-2 and the `name-only` code.

Pro-include: a randomised single-blind crossover in 15 healthy adults in which resting energy expenditure and RER were measured over 3 h postprandially by indirect calorimetry — postprandial EE after an acute protein bolus is the same measurement class as TEF, which §2 condition 3 lists, and it is exactly the kind of record the recall rebuild exists to stop missing. Flagging rather than concurring because it is the only human record in the pumpkin batch, and its exclusion depends on reading §2.3(B) framing and §3's component rule the same way twice.

author_reason: The one overturned exclusion. Randomised double-blind crossover, 12 healthy women, acute oral ingestion of 90 g wild watermelon extract juice, with blood flow in the posterior tibial artery significantly increased against placebo at 30/60/90 min supine. All four conditions hold on the abstract's own text, and the bed is an extremity one, which 2.3 lists among those peripheral circulation reaches and whose rationale calls the substrate of felt warmth. This record had been excluded by the 2026-08-08 author sweep citing the reactivity-probe rule, but none of that rule's named triggers is present: no occlusion, no pharmacological probe, no flow-mediated dilatation. Of the 39 limb- or skin-bed records that sweep excluded, every other one carries an organ or skeletal-muscle bed or a named probe, so restoring this one removes an inconsistency rather than making one. The paper frames itself on arterial stiffness and nitric oxide rather than warmth, but 2.3 makes the bed and the probe decisive, and rewriting that rule once it is known which record it decides is the failure this protocol exists to prevent.

third_reason: §2.3(B) energy expenditure — genuinely on the line. Applied strictly the framing test fails and the exclusion stands; I flag it rather than concur because the disqualifier is vocabulary alone and the full text may state a thermogenesis framing. Recommend author check of the full text's calorimetry rationale.
